title: Siegard distribution manifest
description: Contract for siegard-manifest.json at the plugin root. It is one of exactly two records an installation carries, and fixes what it owns: everything except the identity, description, and version that plugin.json holds. R12 lists the fields, and this contract holds exactly those: no timestamp, because a value the generator minted would differ between two runs over identical source and R4 calls that a defect. R13 makes it the only thing a consumer reads besides the plugin version, so nothing here may require inspecting a component's contents to interpret. R14 makes it the provenance record an upgrade diffs against, which is why every installed path carries a digest: an upgrade that could not tell a consumer's edit from a framework change would have to overwrite or guess, and R17 forbids both. R15 keeps it distinct from the generation manifest, which answers where a generation put things rather than what is installed here.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects a manifest it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

source_revision.description: . The framework source commit this distribution was built from. Reproducing a distribution needs the source it came from; a manifest that named only a version could not distinguish two builds of the same version.

generator_version.description: the output a function of the framework source AND the generator, so R12 records both. A difference in output traced to neither would be the nondeterminism R4 calls a defect.

installed.description: every installed path. R5 requires each to originate in framework source, and R14 makes this the state an upgrade diffs against.

path.description: Plugin-root-relative path of the installed file. Never absolute and never traversing: a manifest entry is also an instruction to an installer, and one naming a path outside the plugin root would be an instruction to write there.

source.description: The repository-relative framework source this file came from. no file is introduced that has no source. A generated file with no source would be one nothing can regenerate.

digest.description: Content hash of the installed file. What is required: an upgrade to detect a file the consumer changed and stop rather than overwrite it; without a recorded digest there is nothing to detect it against.

schemas.description: the contract version of every schema shipped. A consumer selects behaviour on these rather than on what a schema file happens to contain.

path.description: Plugin-root-relative path of the shipped schema.

capabilities.description: each capability's lifecycle status. What is required: status to be derived from checkable facts rather than maintained by hand, and R14 makes `deprecated` observable from an installation rather than only from a release — this field is where a consumer observes it.

name.description: The capability's stable identifier, as the harness invokes or resolves it.

class.description: The capability class, from the closed set of six. A component fitting none of them is not shipped until a class for it exists.

status.description: The capability's lifecycle status. `proposed` ships nothing, so it never appears here; `retired` is absent from the distribution, so it never appears here either. The enum is complete rather than reduced because the transition through `deprecated` must be expressible.

path.description: Plugin-root-relative path of the component that carries this capability.

declaration.description: The declaration this capability carries, derived from the authored set rather than written here. `identifier` and `class` are absent because the entry around it already holds both. This is the only way a declaration reaches a consumer: the authored file is not installed. The parts required here are the ones every capability class must declare; the full contract is `capability-declaration/1` and is enforced where the set is authored, so this checks that a derived entry carries the parts rather than restating a contract that would then have two homes. Absent where the capability carries no declaration yet.

overrides.description: every declared override. the case this exists for — a consumer replaces a shipped template by declaring it here, so a later upgrade can tell a customization from a divergence and stop rather than overwrite. Empty in a freshly generated distribution: the framework declares none, and only an installation acquires them.

reason.description: Why it was replaced. An override with no stated reason is indistinguishable from a divergence nobody meant, which is the pair exists to keep apart.
